clue.text: Restaurant takeaway for a bitch in here?

blocks.note: surface reading: a container for leftovers carried home from a meal out
setter's reading: a bitch is a female dog, so this is a sack fit to hold a hound

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about where a woman might be stuffed after dinner out.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitch looks like an insult but is the literal female dog, which makes the leftovers bag sound like a home for a canine.
explanation.definitionFit: Restaurants hand diners a bag for uneaten food, nominally meant for feeding the family pet.

clue.text: Head removed from piss-artist by a Salome?

indicators.note: taking the head off a word means dropping its first letter

blocks.note: a toper is a heavy drinker, as is a piss-artist in British slang
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk losing his head over Salome, who famously had a head removed.
explanation.walkthrough: Salome is the Richard Strauss work, so the question mark marks a definition by example; a piss-artist is British slang for a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Strauss's Salome is a well-known example of a sung stage drama, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Bang in the middle of huge tit once

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning their joins

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Something exploding in the middle of a giant breast, once upon a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang phrases meaning to have sex with someone.

clue.text: Pissed, beer on tie – curse!

indicators.note: drunk words stagger about, so the following letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk spills beer down his tie and swears.
explanation.definitionFit: A bete noire is a pet hate, a thing that plagues one, like a curse or bane.

clue.text: (& 17dn.) Pious-free shit

blocks.note: a pious person is virtuous
free of charge

explanation.surface: A sneer at someone who has thrown off religion as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Pious-free' is a red herring: it is not 'without piety' but two separate parts of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a shit and calling them a worthless layabout are both insults for a useless person.

clue.text: One dead old politician's things one comes out with

blocks.note: one as the indefinite article, then the abbreviation for dead used in genealogies
Lib is short for Liberal, a party superseded by the Lib Dems, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A dead former MP's possessions, the stuff he blurts out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-libs are remarks improvised on the spot, things a speaker blurts spontaneously.

clue.text: Nancy boy at heart grabbed by star queer

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
queer in its old sense of odd, so the preceding word is put in an odd order
being grabbed means being held inside the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
the central letter of a three-letter word

explanation.surface: An effeminate young man in the clutches of an unconventional celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy boy looks like a single insult; Nancy alone is the definition. Nancy Astor was the first woman to take a seat in the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Astor, Viscountess Astor, was the first woman MP to sit in Parliament, so her forename leads to the surname.

clue.text: Lazy git acted like Archer around a president

indicators.note: one word wraps around the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: Jeffrey Archer, novelist and peer, was jailed for perjury
Abe is Abraham Lincoln, a US president

explanation.surface: A slothful man behaving like a notorious politician toward a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, the Tory novelist, went to prison in 2001 for perjury, a stock Private Eye target.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-abed is someone who stays in bed late, an idle slugabed or lazy person.

clue.text: To perform fellatio requires light aid and a hot tool

blocks.note: slang verb for oral sex on a man
a hand lamp that helps you see

explanation.surface: A smutty observation that oral sex needs lighting and a sexy partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A hot tool' sounds like part of the sexual scene but is a plain description of a flame-throwing gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumber's or welder's gas burner that produces an intense flame is literally a heated implement.

clue.text: Musicians' testes pointlessly mangled – adults only allowed in

definitions.note: a plural noun defining a single group of six players

indicators.note: without a point of the compass, so one of the letters for north, south, east or west is dropped
something mangled is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
being let in means going inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
an X certificate film was for adults only

explanation.surface: Crushed private parts in a musical group, with an adults-only warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Pointlessly removes S, a compass point, from testes before the rest is rearranged; X was the old British certificate for adult-only films.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of six players performing together is one ensemble of instrumentalists.

clue.text: Getting down to work, or knocking off?

blocks.note: first meaning: busy at one's work
second meaning: British slang for having sex

explanation.walkthrough: Knocking off looks like the opposite of working (stopping for the day), but here it is British slang for having sex, which the answer also means.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both while working and, in British slang, in the act of sexual intercourse.

clue.text: ( &12/21dn.) Bilaterally clubbing bisexual

blocks.note: first meaning: wielding the bat for two opposing teams, as in cricket
second meaning: slang for being attracted to ... sexes

explanation.walkthrough: Clubbing hints at nightlife but refers to swinging a bat; the literal cricket phrase became slang for bisexuality.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing for two teams at once literally, and figuratively being attracted to men and women alike.

clue.text: (see 11ac.)
Limit French to one unfinished row

indicators.note: a word left unfinished loses its final letter

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written
a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: Restricting the French to a single half-built row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier is a border or boundary, the outer limit of a territory or field.

clue.text: Toss sailor, declared gay and laugh socks off

blocks.note: to toss or roll a die
AB, able-bodied seaman
someone out has openly declared their sexuality

explanation.surface: A sailor comes out and his shipmates fall about laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: To roll about is to be helpless with mirth, an idiom for uproarious hilarity.

clue.text: Like an alcoholic drink, the police? Yer, like crazy!

indicators.note: behaving crazily, the word before goes into a mad order

blocks.note: the Criminal Investigation Department, British plain-clothes detectives
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk slurs about the police wanting a drink, yeah, like crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cidery describes something tasting or smelling of fermented apple juice, an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: BBC owe Deb broadcast – showing signs of long neglect

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The BBC owes a debutante a broadcast, a long-neglected debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders' webs gather in corners left untouched, so being draped in them shows long disuse.

clue.text: Go down on Prince Jab

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a lunge is a sudden thrust or jab

explanation.surface: A smutty instruction to perform oral sex on royalty, with a jab thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go down on' reads as sexual slang, but the definition stops at 'Go down' and 'on' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to drop or dive steeply downwards, descend suddenly.

clue.text: (see 5dn.)
Pisspoor balls on youth

blocks.note: balls in British slang means nonsense
Y as in YMCA, Young Men's Christian Association

explanation.surface: A young man's testicles judged dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls looks anatomical but is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal adjectives for something of very low quality, worthless and shoddy.

clue.text: Speaker's place to stick pole in bollocks? Strange

indicators.note: to stick something into another thing puts it inside
completes the instruction: the first piece goes inside the second

blocks.note: both are slang for nonsense
S for south, one of the poles
rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a lectern where you poke a pole into someone's privates.
explanation.walkthrough: Bollocks looks anatomical but is slang for nonsense; rum is British for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform from which an orator addresses an audience.

clue.text: Lists at back of book popular date with old lovers

blocks.note: fashionable, in vogue
standard abbreviation
former partners

explanation.surface: A well-liked person going out with former flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphabetical keys to topics and page numbers are printed at the end of a volume.

clue.text: Expulsion of arse, a worthless sort

blocks.note: first meaning: wind let out from the backside
second meaning: a contemptible person

explanation.walkthrough: Arse is British for backside; the second meaning is the insult used of a tiresome person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both breaking wind and a boring, contemptible individual.

clue.text: Endlessly pussy-whipped people who reach climax (they could get hooked on knickers)

definitions.text: they could get hooked on knickers

indicators.note: with no ending, the final letter is cut off
whipped like cream, the letters are beaten into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written
those who reach the end, the climax of a story

explanation.surface: Henpecked men forever climaxing over lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pussy-whipped' looks like one word but splits into fodder and indicator. In Britain suspenders are the straps that hold up stockings, not trouser braces.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocking suspenders clip onto hosiery and hang from a garter belt worn with underwear.

clue.text: (see 11ac.)
Right bog: not in, not of the city

indicators.note: says that a particular pair of letters is to be left out

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
bog is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A proper countryside toilet, nothing urban about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Not in removes the letters I and N from a gents' toilet; bog is British slang for loo.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means belonging to the countryside, the opposite of urban.

clue.text: Spent long ago, Lords broken up without European agreement

definitions.note: a phrase describing the coin rather than a noun for it

indicators.note: something broken up is in pieces, so these letters are rearranged
without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
the French word for yes

explanation.surface: The House of Lords collapses after failing to reach a deal with Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Without here means outside, not lacking. The definition is cryptic: the coin is something that was spent long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The louis d'or was a gold coin of pre-revolutionary France, currency used and circulated centuries back.

clue.text: Barker's pants

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to a dog of a German breed, a barker
second meaning: loose shorts worn as men's underwear

explanation.walkthrough: Barker's looks like a surname (Ronnie Barker, the comedian) but is a dog's; pants are British underwear, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is a breed of dog, and boxers are loose underpants modelled on fighters' shorts.

clue.text: Old forms of transport luvvies are at home on?

blocks.note: first meaning: stagecoaches, horse-drawn passenger vehicles
second meaning: theatre platforms where actors perform

explanation.walkthrough: Luvvies is British slang, mildly mocking, for theatrical actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage is short for stagecoach, and actors perform on the raised floor of a theatre.

clue.text: Not how ladettes behave – usually swallowing the chief of drugs, Ecstasy

indicators.note: the chief of a word is its leading letter
a word that swallows something holds it inside

blocks.note: for the most part
leading letter
E is slang for the drug

explanation.surface: Wild young women out on the town, usually dropping pills.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladettes are boisterous, hard-drinking young British women, so they behave the opposite way.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting modestly means behaving with decorum and restraint, the opposite of loud laddish excess.
